source: Expected bytes come from a scratch python model of VectorStore::from_records + write: records key[32] | stored record, sorted ascending by key bytes, header ORBVEC | 1 | model | dims | count. The 200-text case proves the hex-string array/sort orders bytewise. The file reads, resolve and persist steps are stubbed by feeding the events they would answer; real file effects run in the byte-parity test against the Rust command.

cases.id: a handful of texts sorted by key bytes
two hundred random texts come out in strict bytewise key order
a long model name and wider vectors
a missing record refuses naming the first wanted key for that text
nothing wanted refuses and reads nothing

payload.detail: the package has no organism or capability text to snapshot

cases.id: a missing output file moves on to the locked snapshot
with no locked snapshot the resolve starts at once with the output as the only snapshot
a locked snapshot equal to the output is not read twice
the locked snapshot is appended after the output
a vector width that does not fit its two-byte header is refused as an encode failure

payload.error: the snapshot cannot be encoded: a vector digest could not be computed or a header field does not fit its width
